beats.text: Franklin ran his days to a strict timetable.
beats.note: The timetable is real. It is in his autobiography.

beats.text: Up at five. Asleep at ten.
beats.note: It opened with a question: "What good shall I do this day?" It closed with another: "What good have I done to day?"

beats.text: "My scheme of Order gave me the most trouble."
beats.note: Order was the virtue that asked every part of his business to have its allotted time.

beats.text: He told a story about a speckled ax.
beats.note: A man tires of polishing it and accepts it while it is still only speckled. Franklin admits he was tempted the same way.

beats.text: He never arrived at the perfection he sought.
beats.note: But he judged himself "a better and a happier man than I otherwise should have been".

beats.text: The famous schedule was a target, not a record.
